title: Multifractality at the Integer Quantum Hall Transition: Acquittal of the Parabolic Law
authors: Sen Mu, Abbas Ali Saberi, Martin R. Zirnbauer
abstract: Stationary wave functions at the integer quantum Hall transition are known to be multifractal, but the exact form of the multifractality spectrum has remained a subject of debate. While conformal field theory arguments predict a parabolic law, numerical simulations show deviations from parabolicity. We resolve this discrepancy by pointing out that powers of the local wave intensity fail to obey the Gaussian Free Field and Abelian Fusion Hypothesis assumed in earlier analysis. Rather, due to the non-Abelian nature of the underlying effective field theory, wave intensity correlators are dressed by insertions of background charge distributed uniformly in space. An exact expression for the $q$-moments of point-contact generated eigenstates is presented. Numerical tests are performed for the critical Chalker-Coddington network model on a rectangular torus. Our results are in precise agreement with the predictions of conformal symmetry realized as a level-4 current algebra.
summary: This paper tackles the multifractality spectrum at the IQH transition, resolving a conflict between theory and simulation. The authors show that standard CFT assumptions are incomplete because they neglect non-Abelian effects, which manifest as a 'dressing factor' in the correlation functions. By incorporating this factor, they reconcile theoretical predictions with numerical results from lattice models.
main_problem: The paper resolves a conflict between Conformal Field Theory (CFT) predictions of a parabolic multifractality law and numerical simulations concerning the wave function scaling at the Integer Quantum Hall (IQH) transition.
main_result: The discrepancy arises because earlier analyses incorrectly assumed Abelian fusion; the true physics requires incorporating a non-Abelian 'dressing factor' into the correlators, leading to agreement with predictions from a level-4 current algebra.
method: Analytical derivation of scaling limits for $q$-moments using Green's functions on a torus geometry, complemented by numerical simulations on the Chalker–Coddington network model.
model_or_system: The Integer Quantum Hall (IQH) transition in 2D disordered topological matter. The primary computational tool is the Chalker–Coddington (CC) network model simulated on a rectangular torus.
key_observables: The $q$-moments of point-contact generated eigenstates, $\langle |\psi_c(\mathbf{o})|^{2q} angle$, and the scaling function $M_q(\mathbf{c}, \mathbf{o})$.
important_parameters: The exponent $q$ (related to moment order), system size ($L$), and the geometry of the torus ($\Sigma = S^1 	imes S^1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis modifies the Gaussian Free Field Hypothesis by introducing a dressing factor $S_q(\mathbf{c}, \mathbf{o})$ due to non-Abelian effects, challenging the initial assumption that simple scaling laws suffice.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows Weyl symmetry checks for wave-intensity moments on a torus. Figure 2 compares numerically scaled data against theoretical predictions, highlighting the necessity of the dressing factor $S_q$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the conflict (CFT vs. simulation) to deriving an exact analytical expression incorporating a dressing factor ($M_q \propto e^{G\Delta_q} S_q$). It then performs numerical tests on the CC model, showing that fitting without $S_q$ leads to incorrect scaling dimensions.
why_interesting: The work provides deep insights into how non-Abelian symmetries modify critical exponents in disordered systems, offering a theoretical framework applicable to other strongly correlated or topological quantum materials where simple CFT predictions fail.
